verses.zh: 耶 和 華 啊 ， 求 你 記 念 我 們 所 遭 遇 的 事 ， 觀 看 我 們 所 受 的 凌 辱 。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] O Lord, reflect on[NOTE:2] what has happened to us;consider[NOTE:3] and look at[NOTE:4] our disgrace.
notes: The speaking voice is now that of a choir singing the community’s lament in the first person plural. The poem is not an alphabetic acrostic like the preceding chapters but has 22 verses, the same as the number of letters in the Hebrew alphabet.

The basic meaning of זָכַר (zakhar) is “to remember, call to mind” (HALOT 270 s.v. I זכר). Although often used of recollection of past events, זָכַר (zakhar, “to remember”) can also describe consideration of present situations: “to consider, think about” something present (BDB 270 s.v. 5), hence “reflect on,” the most appropriate nuance here. Verses 1-6 describe the present plight of Jerusalem. The parallel requests הַבֵּיט וּרְאֵה (habbet ureʾeh, “Look and see!”) have a present-time orientation as well. See also 2:1 and 3:19-20.

Heb “Look!” Although often used in reference to visual perception, נָבַט (navat, “to look”) can also refer to cognitive consideration and mental attention shown to a situation: “to regard” (e.g., 1 Sam 16:7; 2 Kgs 3:14), or “to pay attention to, consider” (e.g., Isa 22:8; 51:1, 2).
Although normally occurring in reference to visual sight, רָאָה (raʾah) is often used in reference to cognitive processes and mental observation. See the note on “Consider” at 2:20.

verses.zh: 我 們 是 無 父 的 孤 兒 ； 我 們 的 母 親 好 像 寡 婦 。
verses.en: We have become fatherless orphans;our mothers have become widows.

verses.zh: 我 們 出 錢 才 得 水 喝 ； 我 們 的 柴 是 人 賣 給 我 們 的 。

Heb “Our inheritance” or “Our inherited possessions/property.” The term נַחֲלָה (nakhalah) has a range of meanings: (1) “inheritance,” (2) “portion, share” and (3) “possession, property.” The land of Canaan was given by the Lord to Israel as its inheritance (Deut 4:21; 15:4; 19:10; 20:16; 21:23; 24:4; 25:19; 26:1; Josh 20:6) and distributed among the tribes, clans, and families (Num 16:14; 36:2; Deut 29:7; Josh 11:23; 13:6; 14:3, 13; 17:4, 6, 14; 19:49; 23:4; Judg 18:1; Ezek 45:1; 47:22; 48:29). Through the land, the family provided an inheritance (property) to its children, with the firstborn receiving pride of position (Gen 31:14; Num 27:7-11; 36:3, 8; 1 Kgs 21:3, 4; Job 42:15; Prov 19:14; Ezek 46:16). Here the parallelism between “our inheritance” and “our homes” would allow for the specific referent of the phrase “our inheritance” to be (1) land or (2) material possessions, or given the nature of the poetry in Lamentations, to carry both meanings at the same time.

verses.en: Our skin is as hot as an ovendue to a fever from hunger.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 敵 人 在 錫 安 玷 污 婦 人 ， 在 猶 大 的 城 邑 玷 污 處 女 。
verses.en: They raped[NOTE:1] women in Zion,virgins in the towns of Judah.

verses.zh: 他 們 吊 起 首 領 的 手 ， 也 不 尊 敬 老 人 的 面 。
verses.en: Princes were hung by their hands; elders were mistreated.[NOTE:1]

verses.en: The elders are gone from the city gate;the young men have stopped playing their music.

verses.zh: 我 們 心 中 的 快 樂 止 息 ， 跳 舞 變 為 悲 哀 。
verses.en: Our hearts no longer have any joy;[NOTE:1] our dancing is turned to mourning.

verses.zh: 冠 冕 從 我 們 的 頭 上 落 下 ； 我 們 犯 罪 了 ， 我 們 有 禍 了 ！
verses.en: The crown has fallen from our head;woe to us, for we have sinned!

verses.zh: 這 些 事 我 們 心 裡 發 昏 ， 我 們 的 眼 睛 昏 花 。
verses.en: Because of this, our hearts are sick;[NOTE:1] because of these things, we can hardly see[NOTE:2] through our tears.[NOTE:3]

verses.en: For wild animals[NOTE:1] are prowling over Mount Zion,which lies desolate.

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 啊 ， 你 存 到 永 遠 ； 你 的 寶 座 存 到 萬 代 。
verses.en: But you, O Lord, reign forever;your throne endures from generation to generation.

verses.zh: 你 為 何 永 遠 忘 記 我 們 ？ 為 何 許 久 離 棄 我 們 ？
verses.en: Why do you keep on forgetting[NOTE:1] us?Why do you forsake us so long?

verses.en: Bring us back to yourself, O Lord, so that we may return[NOTE:1] to you;renew our life[NOTE:2] as in days before,[NOTE:3]
